correctness.rationale: For smooth connected genus-five Artin–Schreier covers in characteristic three, RH partitions sum(m_i+1)=7 and m_i prime to 3, forcing jumps (4,1) or (2,1,1). In the two-pole case normalize y^3−y=x^4+a x²+b x+c/x (c≠0). Local valuations at infinity (-3,-4,4) for x,y,dx and at zero (3,-1,4) show the five forms dx/x, dx, x dx, y dx/x, y dx form a regular basis. Cartier identities yield C(dx/x)=dx/x, C(dx)=C(xdx)=0, C(y dx/x)=y dx/x, C(y dx)=−c^{1/3}dx/x−a^{1/3}dx, so its semilinear rank is three iff a≠0 else two, giving a-number two/three. Independent Laurent-Cartier reimplementation checked all 18 F3 specializations and the symbolic dependence on a. Three-pole p-rank four and genus five force a-number one. The Pries–Zhu partition dimensions give two-pole dimension3 and three-pole dimension4; coefficient divisor a=0 in A²×Gm has dimension2 and is reduced there. On underlying curves the cover-to-curve map has finite fibers, so dimensions 4,3,2 apply to a=1,2,3 respectively.

originality.rationale: The p-rank/ramification partitions and their dimensions were known from Pries–Zhu, while Farnell–Pries constant-Cartier-rank condition p≡1 mod lcm(4,1) does not hold at p=3. Duque-Rosero et al. 2026 same genus/characteristic invariants tables include (4,1),(2,1,1) and dimensions 3,4, but their inspected section and table concern invariant rings, not Cartier a-number jump. Result is the coefficient-sensitive transition and complete a-stratification, qualified for unindexed older Cartier computations.
